subcategory_text: Data processing is mapped, illustrating the data actions and associated data elements for systems/products/services, including components; roles of the component owners/operators; and interactions of individuals or third parties with the systems/products/services.
informative_references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PM-12 (Plan of Action and Milestones Process); NIST SP 800-122 §3.1 (PII Inventory)
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.10 (Acceptable use of information)
GDPR Art. 30 (Records of processing activities), Art. 35 (DPIA)
Aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-03 (data flow mapping)
implementation_examples: Build and maintain data-flow diagrams that link data actions, data elements, system components, roles, and individual/third-party interactions for each processing activity
Use the data-flow map as the authoritative input for DPIA and privacy-risk assessment
Reconcile the data-flow map against the inventory to identify undocumented flows (shadow processing)
assessment_objectives: Determine whether data-flow maps exist for each processing activity
Determine whether maps link data actions to data elements to roles to interactions
Determine whether data-flow maps are inputs to privacy-impact assessments
Determine whether unmapped/shadow flows are detected through reconciliation
